name: Yttrium barium copper oxide
summary: High-temperature superconductor with a rare feature: the oxygen content delta is a genuine, reversible chemical actuation route that shifts Tc from 0 to 93 K. At the same time it is the material whose mechanism has remained unexplained for forty years, and thus a target problem for quantum simulation.

degrees_of_freedom.description: delta in YBa2Cu3O7-delta; controls the hole doping of the CuO2 planes
Josephson coupling between the planes; can be driven optically

inputs.notes: Reversible by annealing in an oxygen atmosphere. One of the few reversible chemical actuation routes in the data set.

couplings.source: Jorgensen et al., Phys. Rev. B 41, 1863 (1990)

couplings.notes: Two plateaus instead of a smooth curve: the 90 K plateau up to delta of about 0.2, the 60 K plateau between 0.3 and 0.45, superconductivity vanishing at the orthorhombic-tetragonal transition near delta = 0.65. The support points from v0.1 were clearly too high at three points.

couplings.source: Wu et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 58, 908 (1987)

validity.condition: 77 K, coated conductor tape, self-field about 3e10 A/m^2

couplings.source: Typical values for commercial REBCO coated conductors

validity.condition: above Tc, driving apical oxygen modes

couplings.source: Kaiser et al., Phys. Rev. B 89, 184516 (2014); Hu et al., Nature Materials 13, 705 (2014), doi:10.1038/nmat3963

couplings.notes: The scale factor of 12 meV could not be verified from the cited works and is to be treated as a placeholder.

states.label: normal state above Tc, pseudogap regime
transiently enhanced interlayer coherence above Tc
states.source: Kaiser et al. (2014); Hu et al. (2014)

transitions.notes: Trigger corrected relative to v0.1: at delta = 0.35 the 60 K plateau applies; optimal doping is reached only below delta of about 0.15.

driven_states.emergent_property: transient Josephson plasma edge above Tc, an indication of induced interlayer coherence
driven_states.source: Hu et al., Nature Materials 13, 705 (2014), doi:10.1038/nmat3963
driven_states.notes: Better documented than the K3C60 case, because the Josephson plasma edge is a more specific signal. The interpretation is nevertheless not conclusive.
driven_states.measured_quantity: Josephson plasma edge in the c-axis reflectivity

drive.polarization: E parallel c, apical oxygen mode

driven_states.emergent_property: Under the same drive conditions that produce superconductivity-like c-axis optics, a time-dependent magnetic field enhancement is measured outside the sample at its edge (Faraday rotation in an adjacent GaP layer), interpreted as transient field expulsion with a volume susceptibility of about -0.3.
driven_states.notes: So far the ONLY positive Meissner-like measurement in the entire field - and it is indirect: the field is not measured inside the sample but at the edge in a neighbouring crystal, and the susceptibility follows from a geometric assumption. Michael, De Santis, Demler and Lee (arXiv:2410.12919) derive edge currents from a flux-Floquet instability of the sine-Gordon model that produce a huge dynamical PARAmagnetic magnetization with the same signal sign - that is, without field expulsion. No independent reproduction as of August 2026. In addition: a photoinduced in-plane gap of about 30 cm^-1, Rosenberg et al., Phys. Rev. B 112, 214522 (2025).
driven_states.measured_quantity: Faraday rotation in an adjacent GaP layer at the sample edge

driven_states.emergent_property: Enhancement of charge density wave order after quenching the superconductivity: the CDW correlation length nearly doubles within about one picosecond. Interpretation: superconductivity stabilizes CDW defects, and removing them makes the CDW more coherent.
driven_states.notes: Not a hidden state - no new periodicity emerges, only increased coherence of the existing CDW. Included because light-induced ENHANCEMENT of order is a class of its own. Cuprate-specific alternative interpretations (transient redistribution of spectral weight) are not excluded.
driven_states.measured_quantity: resonant X-ray scattering, CDW correlation length

gaps: The mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity is unexplained. All edges of this entry are phenomenological; none is derived from first principles.
This gap is precisely the target problem of Fermi-Hubbard simulation on QPUs. The entry is therefore less a description than an open order.
Jc values apply to coated conductors with artificial pinning centers, not to single crystals.
The starting state insulating_af is only reached above delta of about 0.65; the transition t_sc therefore skips over the 60 K plateau as a state in its own right. Intermediate states belong in v0.2.
The field expulsion result is the only positive Meissner-like measurement in the field, measured indirectly and with a worked-out counter-theory. Do not read it as evidence of superconductivity.
The normal state was missing from states[] in v0.1, so two driven states referenced a host state that did not exist. Added.
